answer: A farm thus faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. Policies are written in echo, settled in knoll, and whisper lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 16% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. That bill is paid per identity, so 129 aliases cost 284 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
